Necrosis refers to the cellular changes that occur during
cell death. Diﬀ erent types of necrosis will occur in diﬀ erent 
organs or tissues and often will indicate the cause of cell death.
Coagulation necrosis, caseous necrosis, gangrenous necrosis, 
and liquefaction necrosis are all speciﬁ c terms describing the 
process of cell death.
Apoptosis is a diﬀ erent pattern of cell death. Th is form of cell
death appears to be genetically programmed, which allows for 
removal of cells in a systematic, orderly fashion. For example,
this is the process that organizes removal of cells after inﬂ am-
mation. Likewise, when a woman stops breastfeeding, apoptosis 
directs actions that clear cells that are no longer needed from
the breasts.
